content:
Hi all! We’ve officially announced the first ever math hackathon (mathathon) Challenge, happening Oct. 30–Nov 1st in Pasadena: https://mathathonchallenge.com/

We’re bringing together around 100 teams of mathematicians for a 40-hour event centered on making meaningful progress on open problems using AI. Anthropic and OpenAI are providing a combined $2M in compute/API credits, alongside support from DARPA, Cognition, and many other companies!

A major goal of the event is to encourage responsible AI-assisted mathematics, especially around transparency, impact, and verification. Participants will document their AI interactions and results, and the main track concludes with oral presentations to independent academic judges rather than simply accepting generated solutions at face value. Everything will be documented at https://mathdb.com/.

We’d especially love participation from the Lean/formalization community. We still need many more professional mathematicians and formal-methods researchers to serve as judges, so please sign up if you’d be interested in judging! :) We are hoping to pay our judges a $1,000 - $2,500 honorarium, pending Caltech’s approval + obtaining new sponsors!

Applications for participants are also open, and we’ll try to provide travel/financial aid to every applicant who needs it, so please don’t let travel costs discourage you from applying. Would be great to have a strong formalization/verification presence there! If you have any questions, feel free to DM me!
Is there a discussion thread for this yet? I'm organizing a team on Discord, but it would be great to also involve folks on Zulip.
Just created one here: #general > Discussion: Caltech Mathathon Challenge
